LDRS 1414.title: Citizen Leadership
LDRS 1414.description: Language, theories, concepts, and competencies associated with practicing effective leadership and social change and developing intercultural and global awareness.

LDRS 1424.title: Citizen Leadership Praxis
LDRS 1424.description: Application of foundational knowledge of leadership, intercultural and global awareness, the social change model, and socially responsible leadership concepts toward a service-learning project.

LDRS 2014.title: Principles of Peer Leadership
LDRS 2014.description: Theories and basic principles associated with being a positive influence on fellow students, identification of contemporary college student issues, leadership skills utilized to motivate peers in teamwork-based scenarios, leadership skills associated with human development, ethics, maintaining community, and conflict in decision making. May be repeated once for a maximum of 6 credits.

LDRS 2964.title: Field Study
LDRS 2964.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits.

LDRS 3104.title: The Dynamics of Leadership
LDRS 3104.description: This course examines advanced leadership theories and leadership effectiveness in todays organizations.

LDRS 3304.title: Elements of Team Leadership
LDRS 3304.description: Develop effectiveness in leading, delegating, and communicating within a team environment. Emphasis on motivation of team members, emotional intelligence, ethical issues, team member dynamics, team management, and effective team processes.

LDRS 4044.title: Leadership Studies Capstone
LDRS 4044.description: Culmination of comprehensive knowledge gained about leadership and social change throughout a students undergraduate career. Involves reflection on collegiate leadership experiences and coursework in the leadership and social change minor. Results in student development of an electronic portfolio (i.e., ePortfolio). Pre: Senior standing.

LDRS 4414.title: Leading with Humility
LDRS 4414.description: Teaches nature and origins of humility, traditional and modern understandings, connections to modern leadership theories/frameworks, application of humility to three dimensions: personal, relational, and community/cultural dimensions. Pre: Sophomore Standing

LDRS 4454.title: Toxic Leadership
LDRS 4454.description: Toxic leadership, impacts and outcomes on leaders, followers, and the organizational environment. Apply problem-based learning through case study analysis, critical thinking and decision-making, and cooperative methods mitigating toxic leadership actions. Explore ethical-based leadership principles. Pre: Sophomore standing.

LDRS 4514.title: Skills for Nonprofit Organizational Leaders
LDRS 4514.description: Skills essential for leading nonprofit organizations. Nonprofit sector, governance, fundraising, financial administration, managing personnel, media communications, strategic planning, and leadership skills. Pre: Junior Standing.

LDRS 4964.title: Field Study
LDRS 4964.description: May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits.

LDRS 5004.title: Ethics in Leader/Follower Relationships
LDRS 5004.description: Exploration of relationship between leaders and followers through an ethical lens, with special attention to relational dynamics, toxic leaders, and moral dilemmas. Insights from courageous followership, intelligent disobedience, and ethical leadership will illuminate followership typologies and surface opportunities to work as moral agents of change. Pre: Graduate Standing.

LDRS 5454.title: Leadership Diverse Contexts
LDRS 5454.description: Identification and definition of leadership in formal and non-formal education settings, communities, & organizations. Prerequisite: Graduate Standing Required

LDRS 5464.title: Leadership in a Global Society
LDRS 5464.description: Identification and development of the personal and professional competencies required for effective leadership in an increasingly global, diverse and multicultural society

LDRS 5534.title: Leading with Cognitive Diversity
LDRS 5534.description: Theoretical perspectives, processes and techniques utilized in creativity and problem solving, both adaptively and innovatively. Understanding popular and evidence-based creativity and its application to problem solving. Individual cognitive preference for working within a prevailing paradigm to effect change in institutional structures. Utilizing coping behavior to successfully work within the context of cognitive diversity and organizational change. Applying leadership strategies to various problems, based on a typology of problems. Pre: Graduate standing.

LDRS 5544.title: Leading Teams through Community Change
LDRS 5544.description: Theory and techniques for leading tactical, creative, and problem-solving teams through change. Role of social capital and adaption-innovation theories. Pre: Graduate standing.

LDRS 5554.title: Leading Social Change
LDRS 5554.description: Theories, processes and strategies employed to facilitate social and organizational change. Roles of change agents with respect to institutional structures, adaption, innovation, and the progression of change. Theoretical perspectives of managing change as applied to the systems and structures associated with society and how organizations operate within these systems and structures. Problem solving, social entrepreneurship, organizational change, and contemporary issues. Pre: Graduate standing.
